capability.summary: Sanitize an HTML string with Bleach's default allowlist
capability.description: Passes one caller-supplied HTML string to bleach.clean and returns sanitized HTML with disallowed markup removed or escaped according to the installed Bleach defaults.
capability.problem_space: In-memory cleanup of untrusted HTML before rendering; not a browser, crawler, or policy authoring tool.

constraint.io_signature: Input: one HTML string; output: JSON object containing clean with the sanitized HTML string.
accepted_inputs: a string containing HTML or plain text
untrusted markup that should be filtered by Bleach defaults
constraint.output_shape: Success is an object with status="success", tool="lib.bleach_sanitize", and clean as the sanitized HTML string returned by bleach.clean. A caught sanitization or input exception produces an object with status="error", tool="lib.bleach_sanitize", and message as the exception string, then exits with code 1.
limitations: uses the installed Bleach default policy; tags and attributes are not configurable through this wrapper
does not parse or return a structured DOM
does not guarantee protection for non-HTML contexts such as JavaScript or CSS

output_contract.description: Sanitized HTML string produced by Bleach's installed default policy.

intent_tags: remove unsafe markup from an HTML string
negative_intents: extract text or fields from HTML
sanitize JavaScript or CSS source code

output_contract.description: Sanitized HTML string produced by Bleach's installed default policy.
